payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in flow-cell designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. At projected 500 MWh-scale manufacturing, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its main limitation is temperature sensitivity: the dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to stop.

payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress negative-electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier higher claim because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to be suspended.
